setting: A student is talking to a financial aid officer about a delay in his scholarship payment.
narrator_intro: Listen to a conversation between a student and a financial aid officer.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Hi, I was awarded the Dean's Scholarship this year, but it still hasn't shown up on my tuition account, and classes start next week.

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Let me pull up your file. I see the award here, but it looks like your enrollment verification form hasn't been submitted yet. That form has to be on file before funds are released.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: I thought I submitted that back in July when I registered for classes.

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Registration and the verification form are actually two separate steps, that's a common mix-up. The form is a short one, it just confirms you're enrolled full-time this term.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Okay, where do I find it?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: It's on the financial aid portal, under 'Required Documents.' Once you submit it, funds usually post to your account within five business days.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Five days should still be before the tuition deadline, right?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: It should be, but to be safe, I'd also suggest requesting a short payment extension from the bursar's office today, just in case there's any delay processing the form.

narrator_outro: Now get ready to answer the questions.

questions.narrator_text: Why does the student visit the financial aid office?

options.A: To ask why his scholarship funds have not been applied yet
options.B: To apply for a new scholarship

questions.explanation: He explains his scholarship hasn't appeared on his account and classes start soon.

questions.narrator_text: What is missing from the student's file, according to the officer?
questions.explanation: She tells him the enrollment verification form has not been submitted, which is required to release funds.

questions.narrator_text: What misunderstanding did the student have?

options.A: He thought registering for classes also counted as submitting the verification form
options.B: He thought the scholarship didn't require any forms
options.C: He believed the deadline had already passed
options.D: He thought the form needed to be mailed instead of submitted online

questions.explanation: He assumed submitting his class registration in July covered the requirement, but the officer clarifies they are separate steps.

questions.narrator_text: Why does the officer suggest contacting the bursar's office as well?

options.A: As a precaution in case the funds are delayed past the tuition deadline
options.B: Because the scholarship has likely been cancelled
options.C: Because the bursar's office handles all scholarship approvals
options.D: Because the student needs to pay his tuition in full regardless

questions.explanation: She recommends a payment extension as a safety measure in case there's any delay processing the form.
